title: Prompting Whisper for Joint Speech Transcription and Diarization
comment: To be presented at the Joint Workshop on HSCMA and CHiME 2026
summary: As part of the MediSpeech project, we aim to develop a system that transcribes and diarizes Dutch conversations between doctors and patients in real-time. In this research (in-progress) we explore ways of efficiently combining Whisper with speaker diarization (SD). After trying to prompt Whisper with text that contains speaker labels, we observed that it is able to insert labels into the transcription with promising accuracy. We continued this line of research by fine-tuning Whisper with speaker-labelled prompts to generate transcriptions in a format similar to that of Serialized Output Training (SOT). Fine-tuning Whisper yielded more consistent speaker IDs across the chunks of long-form audio and improved verbatim transcription. The study uncovered new challenges as Whisper's SD performance suffers because of mistakes that get propagated through prompts and inaccurate timestamps assigned to overlapping speech.

AI.tldr: This in-progress research explores combining Whisper with speaker diarization for real-time Dutch medical conversation transcription by prompting and fine-tuning Whisper with speaker labels, achieving promising accuracy but facing challenges with error propagation and overlapping speech timestamps.
AI.motivation: To develop a real-time system that transcribes and diarizes Dutch doctor-patient conversations as part of the MediSpeech project.
AI.method: Explored prompting Whisper with speaker-labelled text and fine-tuning Whisper with speaker-labelled prompts using a Serialized Output Training (SOT)-like format.
AI.result: Prompting achieved promising label insertion accuracy; fine-tuning yielded more consistent speaker IDs across long-form audio chunks and improved verbatim transcription.
AI.conclusion: The approach shows potential but faces challenges from error propagation through prompts and inaccurate timestamps for overlapping speech.

title: Optimal Transport Audio Distance with Learned Riemannian Ground Metrics
comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, 10 tables. The otadtk toolkit is available at https://github.com/wonwoo-jeong/otadtk
summary: In audio generation evaluation, Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) is a 2-Wasserstein distance with structural constraints for both primitives: the cost is a frozen embedding pullback whose invariance set hides severe artifacts, and the coupling is a Gaussian fit that dilutes rank-1 contamination relative to discrete OT. We propose Optimal Transport Audio Distance (OTAD), which corrects each primitive with one dedicated mechanism -- a residual Riemannian ground-metric adapter for the cost and entropic Sinkhorn optimal transport for the coupling. Across eight encoders under a four-axis protocol, coupling-only comparisons at $ε= 0.05$ show that Sinkhorn's rank-1 sensitivity exceeds FAD's by a factor of 1.9 to 3.6. Furthermore, OTAD achieves a higher mean Spearman correlation with audio-quality MOS (DCASE 2023 Task 7) than baseline metrics. As an intrinsic benefit of the discrete transport plan, OTAD yields per-sample diagnostics with AUROC $\ge 0.86$, a capability that scalar- or kernel-aggregated metrics structurally lack.

AI.tldr: OTAD replaces FAD's flawed Gaussian coupling and frozen embedding cost with Sinkhorn optimal transport and a residual Riemannian ground-metric adapter, achieving higher sensitivity to artifacts, better MOS correlation, and per-sample diagnostic capability (AUROC ≥ 0.86).
AI.motivation: FAD suffers from two structural flaws: (1) its cost uses a frozen embedding pullback whose invariance set hides severe artifacts, and (2) its coupling relies on a Gaussian fit that dilutes rank-1 contamination relative to discrete optimal transport.
AI.method: OTAD corrects FAD's two primitives: (1) a residual Riemannian ground-metric adapter for the cost, and (2) entropic Sinkhorn optimal transport for the coupling. Evaluated across eight encoders under a four-axis protocol.
AI.result: Sinkhorn's rank-1 sensitivity exceeds FAD's by 1.9–3.6× at ε=0.05. OTAD achieves higher mean Spearman correlation with audio-quality MOS (DCASE 2023 Task 7) than baselines. OTAD yields per-sample diagnostics with AUROC ≥ 0.86.
AI.conclusion: OTAD outperforms FAD and other baseline metrics in artifact detection, MOS correlation, and per-sample diagnostic capability, which scalar- or kernel-aggregated metrics structurally lack.

title: NDF+: Joint Neural Directional Filtering and Diffuse Sound Extraction
summary: Recently, neural directional filtering (NDF) has been introduced as a flexible approach for reconstructing a virtual directional microphone (VDM) with a desired directivity pattern for spatial sound capture. Building on this idea, we propose NDF+, which enables joint neural directional filtering and diffuse sound extraction. NDF+ reformulates VDM estimation into two coupled subtasks: dereverberated VDM reconstruction and diffuse sound extraction. This reformulation enables NDF+ to manipulate diffuse components in the final reconstructed VDM output. We evaluated NDF+ under reverberant conditions and compared it with representative conventional baselines. Results show that NDF+ consistently outperforms the baselines on both subtasks, while maintaining VDM reconstruction quality comparable to that of the original single-task NDF model. These findings indicate that NDF+ introduces an additional degree of freedom for diffuse sound control in the VDM reconstruction. In a stereo recording application, NDF+ provides controllable inter-channel level differences between left and right channels by adjusting the estimated diffuse component.

AI.tldr: NDF+ extends neural directional filtering by jointly reconstructing virtual directional microphones and extracting diffuse sound, enabling controllable diffuse components while maintaining high VDM quality.
AI.motivation: To overcome the limitation of the original NDF that cannot manipulate diffuse components in VDM reconstruction, by introducing a joint framework for both directional filtering and diffuse sound extraction.
AI.method: Reformulates VDM estimation into two coupled subtasks: dereverberated VDM reconstruction and diffuse sound extraction, enabling joint neural directional filtering and diffuse sound control.
AI.result: NDF+ consistently outperforms conventional baselines on both subtasks under reverberant conditions, while maintaining VDM reconstruction quality comparable to the single-task NDF model.
AI.conclusion: NDF+ introduces an additional degree of freedom for diffuse sound control in VDM reconstruction, demonstrated by controllable inter-channel level differences in stereo recording applications.

title: Predictive-Generative Drift Decomposition for Speech Enhancement and Separation
summary: We propose a plug-and-play framework for speech enhancement and separation that augments predictive methods with a generative speech prior. Our approach, termed Stochastic Interpolant Prior for Speech (SIPS), builds on stochastic interpolants and leverages their flexibility to bridge predictive and generative modeling. Specifically, we decompose the interpolation dynamics into a task-specific drift and a stochastic denoising component, allowing a predictive estimate to be integrated directly into the generative sampling process. This results in a mathematically grounded framework for combining strong pretrained predictors with the expressive power of generative models. To this end, we train a score model using only clean speech, yielding a degradation-agnostic prior that can be reused across tasks. During inference, the predictor provides a deterministic drift that steers the sampling process toward a task-consistent estimate, while the score model preserves perceptual naturalness. Unlike prior hybrid approaches, which typically rely on architecture-specific conditioning and are tied to particular predictors or degradation settings, SIPS provides a unified framework that generalizes across predictors and additive degradation tasks. We demonstrate its effectiveness for both speech enhancement and speech separation using recent predictors such as SEMamba and FlexIO. The proposed method consistently improves perceptual quality, achieving gains up +1.0 NISQA for speech separation.

AI.tldr: SIPS is a plug-and-play framework that integrates predictive speech enhancement/separation models with a generative speech prior (score model trained on clean speech only) via stochastic interpolants, improving perceptual quality across tasks and predictors without architecture-specific modifications.
AI.motivation: Existing hybrid predictive-generative approaches for speech enhancement are tied to specific architectures, predictors, or degradation settings, lacking a unified framework that generalizes across tasks and predictors while preserving perceptual quality.
AI.method: SIPS decomposes stochastic interpolation dynamics into a task-specific drift (from a pretrained predictor) and a stochastic denoising component (from a score model trained on clean speech). The predictor provides a deterministic drift toward task-consistent estimates, while the score model ensures perceptual naturalness. The score model is degradation-agnostic and reusable across tasks. Inference combines both components in a unified sampling process.
AI.result: The method consistently improves perceptual quality across speech enhancement and separation tasks, achieving up to +1.0 NISQA improvement for speech separation using predictors like SEMamba and FlexIO.
AI.conclusion: SIPS provides a mathematically grounded, unified hybrid framework that generalizes across different predictors and additive degradation tasks, effectively combining predictive accuracy with generative perceptual quality without architecture-specific conditioning.

title: X-Voice: Enabling Everyone to Speak 30 Languages via Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Voice Cloning
summary: In this paper, we present X-Voice, a 0.4B multilingual zero-shot voice cloning model that clones arbitrary voices and enables everyone to speak 30 languages. X-Voice is trained on a 420K-hour multilingual corpus using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) as a unified representation. To eliminate the reliance on prompt text without complex preprocessing like forced alignment, we design a two-stage training paradigm. In Stage 1, we establish X-Voice$_{\text{s1}}$ through standard conditional flow-matching training and use it to synthesize 10K hours of speaker-consistent segments as audio prompts. In Stage 2, we fine-tune on these audio pairs with prompt text masked to derive X-Voice$_{\text{s2}}$, which enables zero-shot voice cloning without requiring transcripts of audio prompts. Architecturally, we extend F5-TTS by implementing a dual-level injection of language identifiers and decoupling and scheduling of Classifier-Free Guidance to facilitate multilingual speech synthesis. Subjective and objective evaluation results demonstrate that X-Voice outperforms existing flow-matching based multilingual systems like LEMAS-TTS and achieves zero-shot cross-lingual cloning capabilities comparable to billion-scale models such as Qwen3-TTS. To facilitate research transparency and community advancement, we open-source all related resources.

AI.tldr: X-Voice is a 0.4B multilingual zero-shot voice cloning model trained on 420K hours of data, using IPA representation and a two-stage training paradigm to eliminate reliance on prompt text transcripts. It extends F5-TTS with dual-level language identifier injection and CFG decoupling, outperforming existing flow-matching multilingual systems and achieving cross-lingual cloning comparable to billion-scale models.
AI.motivation: To create a lightweight (0.4B) multilingual zero-shot voice cloning model that can clone arbitrary voices and enable speaking in 30 languages, while eliminating the need for prompt text transcripts and complex preprocessing like forced alignment.
AI.method: Two-stage training paradigm: (1) Stage 1 trains X-Voice_s1 via conditional flow-matching on 420K-hour multilingual IPA-annotated corpus, then synthesizes 10K hours of speaker-consistent audio prompts. (2) Stage 2 fine-tunes on audio pairs with masked prompt text to produce X-Voice_s2, enabling transcript-free zero-shot cloning. Architecture extends F5-TTS with dual-level language identifier injection and decoupled/scheduled Classifier-Free Guidance.
AI.result: Outperforms existing flow-matching multilingual systems (LEMAS-TTS) and achieves zero-shot cross-lingual cloning capabilities comparable to billion-scale models (Qwen3-TTS).
AI.conclusion: X-Voice provides an effective, lightweight solution for multilingual zero-shot voice cloning without prompt text dependency, and all resources are open-sourced to promote research transparency.

title: Maximal Controlled Invariant-MPC: Enhancing Feasibility and Reducing Conservatism through Terminal CBF Constraint in Safety-Critical Control
summary: Optimal control for safety-critical systems is often dependent on the conservativeness of constraints. Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) serve as a medium to represent such constraints, but constructing a minimally conservative CBF is a computationally intractable problem. Therefore, approaches that can guarantee safety while reducing conservatism will help improve the optimality of the system under consideration. Here, we present a Model Predictive Control (MPC) formulation using CBF as a terminal constraint, which is proven to improve feasibility and reachable sets with increasing prediction horizon. The constructive nature of the proofs allows for warm-starting the nonlinear optimization problem, thereby reducing the computational time substantially. Simulations are set up for a simple nonholonomic system to numerically validate the results, and it is observed that the number of infeasible points decreased by a factor of 1.7 to 2.7. The increase in reachable state space was demonstrated by the ability of the system to track trajectories that are entirely inside the unsafe region of the control barrier function.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an MPC formulation using CBFs as terminal constraints to reduce conservatism in safety-critical control, with theoretical proofs showing improved feasibility and reachable sets as prediction horizon increases, along with a warm-starting strategy that reduces computational time. Simulations with a nonholonomic system show a 1.7-2.7x reduction in infeasible points and expanded reachable state space.
AI.motivation: Optimal control for safety-critical systems is limited by the conservativeness of constraints. CBFs represent such constraints but constructing a minimally conservative CBF is computationally intractable. Therefore, approaches that guarantee safety while reducing conservatism are needed to improve system optimality.
AI.method: The authors formulate an MPC framework with CBFs as terminal constraints. They provide constructive proofs for improved feasibility and reachable sets with increasing prediction horizon, and leverage the constructive nature for warm-starting the nonlinear optimization problem to reduce computational time.
AI.result: For a simple nonholonomic system, the number of infeasible points decreased by a factor of 1.7 to 2.7, and the reachable state space expanded, demonstrated by tracking trajectories entirely inside the unsafe region of the CBF.
AI.conclusion: Using CBFs as terminal constraints in MPC with warm-starting effectively reduces conservatism while guaranteeing safety, improving both feasibility and reachable sets at reduced computational cost.

title: WavCube: Unifying Speech Representation for Understanding and Generation via Semantic-Acoustic Joint Modeling
summary: Integrating speech understanding and generation is a pivotal step toward building unified speech models. However, the different representations required for these two tasks currently pose significant compatibility challenges. Typically, semantics-oriented features are learned from self-supervised learning (SSL), and acoustic-oriented features from reconstruction. Such fragmented representations hinder the realization of truly unified speech systems. We present WavCube, a compact continuous latent derived from an SSL speech encoder that simultaneously supports speech understanding, reconstruction, and generation. WavCube employs a two-stage training scheme. Stage 1 trains a semantic bottleneck to filter off-manifold redundancy that makes raw SSL features intractable for diffusion. Stage 2 injects fine-grained acoustic details via end-to-end reconstruction, while a semantic anchoring loss ensures the representation remains grounded within its original semantic manifold. Comprehensive experiments show that WavCube closely approaches WavLM performance on SUPERB despite an 8x dimensional compression, attains reconstruction quality on par with existing acoustic representations, delivers state-of-the-art zero-shot TTS performance with markedly faster training convergence, and excels in speech enhancement, separation, and voice conversion tasks on the SUPERB-SG benchmark. Systematic ablations reveal that WavCube's two-stage recipe resolves two intrinsic flaws of SSL features for generative modeling, paving the way for future unified speech systems. Codes and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/yanghaha0908/WavCube.

AI.tldr: WavCube is a compact continuous latent representation from an SSL speech encoder that supports speech understanding, reconstruction, and generation via a two-stage training scheme (semantic bottleneck + acoustic detail injection with semantic anchoring), achieving strong performance across SUPERB, zero-shot TTS, speech enhancement, separation, and voice conversion tasks.
AI.motivation: To overcome the compatibility challenge between semantics-oriented features (from SSL) and acoustic-oriented features (from reconstruction) that currently hinders the realization of truly unified speech systems.
AI.method: WavCube employs a two-stage training scheme: (1) Stage 1 trains a semantic bottleneck to filter off-manifold redundancy from raw SSL features; (2) Stage 2 injects fine-grained acoustic details via end-to-end reconstruction while a semantic anchoring loss keeps the representation grounded in its semantic manifold.
AI.result: WavCube approaches WavLM on SUPERB despite 8x dimensional compression, matches existing acoustic representations in reconstruction quality, achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot TTS with faster training convergence, and excels in speech enhancement, separation, and voice conversion on SUPERB-SG.
AI.conclusion: WavCube's two-stage recipe resolves two intrinsic flaws of SSL features for generative modeling, paving the way for future unified speech systems.

title: Do Melody and Rhythm Coevolve?
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, to be included in Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society
summary: Music comprises two core structural components, melody and rhythm, that vary widely across cultures. Whether these components coevolve in a coupled way or follow independent trajectories remains unclear. We introduce a novel computational pipeline to extract vocal melodic pitch-interval and percussive inter-onset timing distributions from 27,628 popular songs across 59 countries, enabling large-scale cross-cultural comparison that bypasses traditional music annotations. Musical similarities between countries aligned with geographic and linguistic relationships, validating our approach. Substantial variation emerged in both melodic and rhythmic structures across countries, yet the diversity of the two components was not significantly correlated, challenging assumptions of coupled evolution. Only rhythmic diversity was significantly associated with ethnic and linguistic heterogeneity, while melodic diversity showed no such association. These findings suggest that melody and rhythm constitute partially independent systems shaped by distinct cultural and evolutionary pressures, rather than components of a single monolithic musical style.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 27,628 songs from 59 countries shows melody and rhythm are partially independent cultural systems, with rhythmic diversity linked to ethnic/linguistic heterogeneity but melodic diversity not, challenging the assumption of coupled evolution between these musical components.
AI.motivation: To determine whether melody and rhythm coevolve in a coupled way or follow independent trajectories across different cultures, challenging existing assumptions about monolithic musical styles.
AI.method: Novel computational pipeline extracting vocal melodic pitch-interval and percussive inter-onset timing distributions from 27,628 popular songs across 59 countries, enabling large-scale cross-cultural comparison without traditional music annotations.
AI.result: Musical similarities between countries aligned with geographic and linguistic relationships. Substantial variation in both melodic and rhythmic structures across countries, but their diversity was not significantly correlated. Only rhythmic diversity was significantly associated with ethnic and linguistic heterogeneity.
AI.conclusion: Melody and rhythm constitute partially independent systems shaped by distinct cultural and evolutionary pressures, rather than components of a single monolithic musical style.

title: Space-Time Diversity in Observability and Estimation on Product Lie Groups
comment: 6 Pages (two columns), 1 figure 2 tables and an alogorithm. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Robust state estimation in coupled dynamical systems depends critically not only on sensor quality but on the structural alignment between observation channels and the system's intrinsic dynamics. This paper develops a rigorous framework for analyzing spatial and temporal diversity in dynamical state estimation on product Lie groups, drawing structural parallels to diversity gains in space-time coding. Three main results are established: (i) coupling-based necessary and sufficient conditions for cross-factor observability, showing that a sensor local to one group factor renders another factor observable if and only if the dynamics propagate error directions across the corresponding Lie algebra components; (ii) a spatial diversity saturation theorem identifying precisely when additional observation channels fail to expand the propagated observation subspace and thus provide no structural benefit; and (iii) a time-space diversity decomposition that exactly separates instantaneous spatial information from accumulated temporal information in the estimation error covariance. The framework is applied to planar SE(2) and spatial SE(3) navigation, yielding exact observability guarantees for redundant and non redundant sensor architectures in modern robotics and autonomous vehicles. These results extend classical observability theory beyond Euclidean state spaces, exposing structural constraints invisible to standard rank-based analysis that fundamentally govern robust inference in coupled dynamical systems.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a framework for analyzing spatial and temporal diversity in dynamical state estimation on product Lie groups, establishing conditions for cross-factor observability, spatial diversity saturation, and time-space diversity decomposition, with applications to SE(2) and SE(3) navigation.
AI.motivation: Robust state estimation in coupled dynamical systems depends on the structural alignment between observation channels and system dynamics, which is poorly captured by standard rank-based observability analysis in non-Euclidean state spaces.
AI.method: The authors develop a rigorous theoretical framework on product Lie groups, drawing parallels to space-time coding diversity gains. They establish coupling-based observability conditions, a spatial diversity saturation theorem, and a time-space diversity decomposition.
AI.result: Three main results: (i) necessary and sufficient conditions for cross-factor observability via coupling in Lie algebra; (ii) identification of when additional sensors provide no structural benefit (diversity saturation); (iii) exact decomposition of instantaneous spatial and accumulated temporal information in error covariance.
AI.conclusion: The framework extends classical observability theory beyond Euclidean spaces, revealing structural constraints invisible to standard rank-based analysis that govern robust inference in coupled dynamical systems, validated on SE(2) and SE(3) navigation.

title: Task-Aware Answer Preservation under Audio Compression for Large Audio Language Models
summary: Large audio language models (LALMs) are increasingly used to reason over long audio clips, yet deployment often compresses audio before inference to reduce memory and latency. The risk is that compression can leave aggregate accuracy acceptable while sharply degrading answers for a deployment-critical query family. We study answer-preserving audio compression, judging a compressor by the excess answer-error it induces, especially for the worst-affected family. We formulate this theoretically as a compressor acceptance-rejection criterion, derive a practical sign-off protocol that returns compression budgets satisfying worst-family checks with statistical confidence, and evaluate it on five multiple-choice audio question-answering benchmarks with two Qwen-based backbones. The protocol exposes hidden family-level damage, shows that the chosen query-family partition can change the approved budget, and identifies regimes where query-conditioned compression helps maintain answer preservation.

AI.tldr: The paper studies answer-preserving audio compression for LALMs, proposing a theoretical criterion and practical protocol to ensure compression doesn't degrade answers for critical query families, with evaluation on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Deploying LALMs with audio compression can degrade answers for deployment-critical query families even when aggregate accuracy appears acceptable, motivating a need for answer-preserving compression guarantees at the family level.
AI.method: Formulates a theoretical compressor acceptance-rejection criterion, derives a practical sign-off protocol that returns compression budgets satisfying worst-family error checks with statistical confidence, and evaluates on five multiple-choice audio QA benchmarks using two Qwen-based backbones.
AI.result: The protocol exposes hidden family-level damage, shows that the chosen query-family partition changes the approved budget, and identifies regimes where query-conditioned compression helps maintain answer preservation.
AI.conclusion: Compression decisions should be validated against worst-case query families rather than aggregate metrics; query-conditioned compression can be beneficial in certain regimes.

title: Quantum Kernels for Audio Deepfake Detection Using Spectrogram Patch Features
summary: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising tool for pattern recognition, yet many audio-focused approaches still treat spectrograms as generic images and do not explicitly exploit their time-frequency structure. We propose Q-Patch, a quantum feature map tailored to audio that encodes local time-frequency patches from mel-spectrograms into quantum states using shallow, hardware-efficient circuits with adjacency-aware entanglement. Each selected patch is summarized by a compact four-dimensional acoustic descriptor and mapped to a four-qubit circuit with depth at most three, enabling practical quantum kernel construction under near-term constraints. We evaluate Q-Patch on an audio spoofing detection task using a controlled, balanced protocol and compare it with size-matched classical baselines. Q-Patch improves discrimination between bona fide and spoofed samples, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.87, compared with 0.82 for a radial basis function support vector machine (RBF-SVM) trained on the same patch-level features. Kernel-space analysis further reveals a clear class structure, with cross-class similarity around 0.615 and within-class self-similarity of 1.00. Overall, Q-Patch provides a practical framework for incorporating time-frequency-aware representations into quantum kernel learning for audio authenticity assessment in low-resource settings.

AI.tldr: Q-Patch is a quantum feature map that encodes local time-frequency patches from mel-spectrograms into quantum states using shallow, hardware-efficient circuits with adjacency-aware entanglement. It achieves superior audio spoofing detection (AUROC 0.87) compared to classical RBF-SVM (0.82) under a controlled protocol.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum machine learning methods for audio treat spectrograms as generic images without exploiting their explicit time-frequency structure.
AI.method: Local time-frequency patches from mel-spectrograms are summarized into compact four-dimensional acoustic descriptors, then mapped to a four-qubit quantum circuit (depth ≤ 3) with adjacency-aware entanglement for kernel construction.
AI.result: Q-Patch achieves AUROC of 0.87 on audio spoofing detection vs. 0.82 for RBF-SVM. Kernel analysis shows cross-class similarity ~0.615 and within-class self-similarity of 1.00.
AI.conclusion: Q-Patch provides a practical framework for incorporating time-frequency-aware representations into quantum kernel learning for audio authenticity assessment in low-resource settings.

title: PianoCoRe: Combined and Refined Piano MIDI Dataset
comment: Published in TISMIR. Project repository: https://github.com/ilya16/PianoCoRe
summary: Symbolic music datasets with matched scores and performances are essential for many music information retrieval (MIR) tasks. Yet, existing resources often cover a narrow range of composers, lack performance variety, omit note-level alignments, or use inconsistent naming formats. This work presents PianoCoRe, a large-scale piano MIDI dataset that unifies and refines major open-source piano corpora. The dataset contains 250,046 performances of 5,625 pieces written by 483 composers, totaling 21,763 h of performed music. PianoCoRe is released in tiered subsets to support different applications: from large-scale analysis and pre-training (PianoCoRe-C and deduplicated PianoCoRe-B) to expressive performance modeling with note-level score alignment (PianoCoRe-A/A*). The note-aligned subset, PianoCoRe-A, provides the largest open-source collection of 157,207 performances aligned to 1,591 scores to date. In addition to the dataset, the contributions are: (1) a MIDI quality classifier for detecting corrupted and score-like transcriptions and (2) RAScoP, an alignment refinement pipeline that cleans temporal alignment errors and interpolates missing notes. The analysis shows that the refinement reduces temporal noise and eliminates tempo outliers. Moreover, an expressive performance rendering model trained on PianoCoRe demonstrates improved robustness to unseen pieces compared to models trained on raw or smaller datasets. PianoCoRe provides a ready-to-use foundation for the next generation of expressive piano performance research.

AI.tldr: PianoCoRe is a large-scale, tiered piano MIDI dataset (250K performances, 5,625 pieces, 483 composers) with score-aligned subsets (up to 157K aligned performances), a MIDI quality classifier, and an alignment refinement pipeline (RAScoP), enabling robust expressive performance modeling and MIR research.
AI.motivation: Existing symbolic music datasets with matched scores and performances suffer from limited composer diversity, lack of performance variety, missing note-level alignments, and inconsistent naming conventions, hindering progress in MIR tasks.
AI.method: The authors unify and refine major open-source piano corpora into a tiered dataset (PianoCoRe-C, -B, -A/A*), develop a MIDI quality classifier to filter corrupted/score-like transcriptions, and propose RAScoP—an alignment refinement pipeline that cleans temporal errors and interpolates missing notes.
AI.result: PianoCoRe contains 250,046 performances of 5,625 pieces by 483 composers (21,763 hours). The note-aligned subset (PianoCoRe-A) is the largest open-source collection of 157,207 performances aligned to 1,591 scores. RAScoP reduces temporal noise and eliminates tempo outliers. An expressive performance rendering model trained on PianoCoRe shows improved robustness to unseen pieces versus raw or smaller datasets.
AI.conclusion: PianoCoRe provides a ready-to-use foundation for expressive piano performance research and future MIR tasks, enabling large-scale pre-training and robust performance modeling.

title: Consideration of Control-Loop Interaction in Transient Stability of Grid-Following Inverters using Bandwidth Separation Method
summary: Grid-following inverters have been widely adopted as a grid interface for renewable energy, and ensuring their small-signal and large-signal stability is critical to modern power systems. Their large-signal, or transient, stability is a significant challenge to analyze because of the interaction of the phase-locked loop (PLL), which must maintain synchronism with various outer-loop controllers. Simple analysis in which outer-loop controllers are idealized is insufficient, and the interactions between the nonlinear dynamics of the PLL and the dynamics of the DC-link voltage control (DVC), as well as the AC terminal voltage control (TVC) when present, must be considered. An asymptotic analysis approach, termed the bandwidth separation method, is proposed. This method enables simplification and order reduction of the original differential equations when sufficient bandwidth separation exists. Through this method, the interaction between the DVC and PLL is explicitly characterized, revealing that such interaction degrades system stability and shrinks the stability region. The analysis also indicates that voltage instability, rather than PLL loss of synchronization alone, is often the root cause of transient instability. Optimal bandwidth configurations for the PLL and DVC are identified under various grid fault conditions: a larger PLL bandwidth improves resilience to phase-jump faults, while a larger DVC bandwidth enhances tolerance to power fluctuations. In addition, the influence of the TVC loop is analyzed, showing that a high TVC bandwidth can mitigate the destabilizing effects of PLL-DVC interaction and further improve transient stability. All analytical findings are validated through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a bandwidth separation asymptotic analysis method to study large-signal (transient) stability of grid-following inverters, revealing how interactions between PLL, DC-link voltage control (DVC), and AC terminal voltage control (TVC) affect stability. Key findings include that PLL-DVC interaction degrades stability, voltage instability often underlies transient instability, and optimal bandwidth configurations improve resilience to different fault types.
AI.motivation: Transient stability of grid-following inverters is a significant challenge due to the complex nonlinear interactions between the PLL and outer-loop controllers (DVC, TVC). Simplified analyses that idealize outer-loop controllers are insufficient, motivating the need for a method that can explicitly characterize these interactions and their impact on stability.
AI.method: The authors propose an asymptotic analysis approach termed the bandwidth separation method, which simplifies and reduces the order of the original differential equations under conditions of sufficient bandwidth separation between controllers. This enables explicit characterization of PLL-DVC interaction and analysis of optimal bandwidth configurations.
AI.result: PLL-DVC interaction degrades system stability and shrinks the stability region. Voltage instability, not PLL loss of synchronization alone, is often the root cause of transient instability. Larger PLL bandwidth improves resilience to phase-jump faults; larger DVC bandwidth enhances tolerance to power fluctuations. High TVC bandwidth can mitigate the destabilizing effects of PLL-DVC interaction.
AI.conclusion: The bandwidth separation method effectively characterizes nonlinear interactions in grid-following inverters. Optimal bandwidth configurations can be identified for different fault conditions to improve transient stability. All analytical findings are validated through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments.

title: Foundation Twins: A New Generation of Power Systems Digital Twins using Foundation AI Models
summary: Power systems are inherently multi-timescale systems, with different physical phenomena and decision-making processes spanning multiple timescales, time horizons, and geographic scopes. I envision power systems digital twins (DTs) as powerful modeling and simulation tools that can accelerate and improve decision-making across different time scales and geographic scopes. However, until now, research has not delivered such a vision, and power systems DTs remain a concept distant from implementation. This is not a regular research paper. This is a position paper that outlines my vision for developing a new generation of power systems DTs that leverage recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). I call these Foundation Twins. Foundation Twins combines the generalization features of foundation models with the decision-making capabilities of reinforcement learning (RL) architectures to deliver the envisioned power systems DTs.

AI.tldr: This position paper proposes "Foundation Twins" — a new generation of power system digital twins that combine foundation models with reinforcement learning to enable multi-timescale, multi-geographic decision-making, addressing the gap between the current vision and practical implementation of power system DTs.
AI.motivation: Power systems are inherently multi-timescale systems, yet existing digital twins have not delivered on the vision of accelerating and improving decision-making across different time scales and geographic scopes. The gap between the conceptual promise and practical implementation motivates the need for a new approach.
AI.method: Foundation Twins combine the generalization capabilities of foundation models (large-scale pre-trained AI models) with the sequential decision-making capabilities of reinforcement learning architectures to create a new generation of power system digital twins.
AI.result: This is a position paper, so no experimental results are reported. The paper presents a conceptual/architectural vision rather than empirical findings.
AI.conclusion: Foundation Twins are proposed as a pathway to realize the long-standing vision of power system digital twins by leveraging recent advances in AI/ML, specifically foundation models and reinforcement learning.

title: Community-to-Vehicle: Integrating Electric Vehicles into Energy Communities -- A Swiss Case Study
summary: The institutional separation between local energy communities and public electric vehicle (EV) charging limits the efficient use of locally generated renewable energy. This paper introduces the concept of community-to-vehicle (C2V) as an institutional design mechanism to bridge this gap by enabling EV charging within the community boundary, where locally generated photovoltaic (PV) surplus is preferentially allocated and offered to external users at a community charging price. Building on the recently introduced local electricity community framework in Switzerland, we design scenarios that capture the transition from full separation to coordinated EV charging and evaluate their impacts on EV users and the community. The results show that C2V significantly improves local PV utilization and enhances economic performance, reducing EV charging costs relative to commercial alternatives while generating additional revenue streams for the community. These findings highlight the potential of C2V as a practical, implementable mechanism for integrating EV charging into local energy communities, providing a clear pathway for adopting coordinated community-EV interaction within existing regulatory frameworks.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes Community-to-Vehicle (C2V) as an institutional mechanism that integrates EV charging into local energy communities by preferentially allocating surplus PV energy to external EV users at a community price, improving local renewable utilization and economic outcomes for both EV users and the community.
AI.motivation: The existing institutional separation between local energy communities and public EV charging prevents efficient utilization of locally generated renewable energy, creating a gap that needs bridging.
AI.method: Building on Switzerland's local electricity community framework, the authors design scenarios transitioning from full separation to coordinated EV charging and evaluate impacts on EV users and the community.
AI.result: C2V significantly improves local PV utilization, reduces EV charging costs compared to commercial alternatives, and generates additional revenue streams for the community.
AI.conclusion: C2V is a practical, implementable mechanism for integrating EV charging into local energy communities within existing regulatory frameworks, providing a clear pathway for coordinated community-EV interaction.

title: SOPF-Based Adaptive Droop Control for Hybrid AC--HVDC Grids Under Offshore Wind Uncertainty
summary: The integration of massive offshore wind into hybrid AC-HVDC grids demands robust DC voltage regulation, yet conventional fixed-gain droop controllers struggle under severe stochastic volatility. This paper bridges the gap between system-level economic dispatch and converter-level control by proposing a novel Stochastic Optimal Power Flow (SOPF)-based adaptive droop framework. Rather than relying on heuristic or reactive tuning, wind forecast uncertainty is modeled using a zone-wise Beta distribution that accurately captures the heteroscedastic nature of wind errors across low, mid, and high power regimes. By leveraging Polynomial Chaos Expansion (PCE) within a chance-constrained SOPF, the system's stochastic states are formulated analytically. Crucially, the optimal adaptive droop gain is extracted directly from the first-order PCE coefficients via a Jacobian-free sensitivity analysis, embedding statistical voltage-security guarantees directly into the local converter control. Validation on a 4-terminal AC-HVDC system demonstrates that scenario-adaptive gains significantly outperform standard fixed-coefficient approaches, effectively minimizing active-power tracking errors during extreme wind disturbances.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Stochastic Optimal Power Flow (SOPF)-based adaptive droop framework for DC voltage regulation in hybrid AC-HVDC grids with massive offshore wind. It models wind forecast uncertainty using a zone-wise Beta distribution, employs Polynomial Chaos Expansion (PCE) within chance-constrained SOPF for analytical state formulation, and extracts optimal adaptive droop gains via Jacobian-free sensitivity analysis from first-order PCE coefficients. Validation on a 4-terminal AC-HVDC system shows superior performance over fixed-gain droop controllers in minimizing active-power tracking errors under extreme wind disturbances.
AI.motivation: Conventional fixed-gain droop controllers fail to provide robust DC voltage regulation under the severe stochastic volatility introduced by massive offshore wind integration into hybrid AC-HVDC grids. There is a gap between system-level economic dispatch and converter-level control that needs to be bridged.
AI.method: A novel SOPF-based adaptive droop framework is developed: (1) wind forecast uncertainty is modeled via a zone-wise Beta distribution capturing heteroscedastic errors across low, mid, and high power regimes; (2) Polynomial Chaos Expansion (PCE) is employed within a chance-constrained SOPF to analytically formulate stochastic system states; (3) optimal adaptive droop gains are extracted from first-order PCE coefficients via Jacobian-free sensitivity analysis, embedding statistical voltage-security guarantees into local converter control.
AI.result: Validation on a 4-terminal AC-HVDC system demonstrates that scenario-adaptive gains significantly outperform standard fixed-coefficient approaches, effectively minimizing active-power tracking errors during extreme wind disturbances.
AI.conclusion: The proposed adaptive droop framework bridges the gap between economic dispatch and converter-level control by embedding statistical voltage-security guarantees directly into local control, offering robust performance under severe wind uncertainty where conventional fixed-gain methods fail.

title: Kirigami-Structured Electronic Capsule for Long-Term Continuous Gastric Monitoring
summary: Ingestible electronic systems enable non-invasive, in situ sensing within the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, yet clinical translation has been limited by uncontrolled transit, short operational lifetimes, and unreliable wireless communication that prevent continuous monitoring. Here, we present a gastric-resident ingestible robotic platform that achieves week-long operation through integration of a bioinspired, electrically triggered release mechanism with a kirigami-enabled electronic architecture. A kirigami-patterned flexible printed circuit board spans the capsule body and deployable superelastic arms, enabling high-density integration of sensing, power management, and wireless modules within a constrained volume while tolerating large mechanical deformation during gastric residence. Stable retention and on-demand disassembly are achieved using thermally responsive polycaprolactone joints that transition from rigid to compliant states under electrical activation, avoiding dependence on variable chemical triggers. Reliable telemetry in the highly attenuating gastric environment is maintained using a dual-band Bluetooth Low Energy and sub-gigahertz module with RSSI- and throughput-aware adaptive transmission, balancing link robustness and energy consumption. We demonstrate long-term, continuous monitoring of gastric radiation exposure, enabling early detection of dose accumulation and providing a promising in vivo alternative to wearable or handheld dosimeters. Swine studies confirm stable gastric residence, sustained real-time telemetry, and safe gastrointestinal passage following triggered disassembly. This work establishes kirigami-enabled integration as a scalable strategy for long-term gastric-resident robotic systems.

AI.tldr: A gastric-resident ingestible robotic platform with kirigami electronics, electrically triggered disassembly, and dual-band adaptive telemetry enables week-long continuous monitoring of GI tract conditions, demonstrated in swine studies for radiation exposure tracking.
AI.motivation: Current ingestible electronic systems face limitations in uncontrolled transit, short operation lifetimes, and unreliable wireless communication that prevent continuous monitoring of the GI tract, hindering clinical translation.
AI.method: The platform integrates: (1) a kirigami-patterned flexible PCB spanning the capsule and deployable superelastic arms for high-density component integration under deformation; (2) thermally responsive polycaprolactone joints enabling electrically triggered on-demand disassembly; (3) dual-band BLE/sub-gigahertz telemetry with RSSI- and throughput-aware adaptive transmission for reliable communication in the attenuating gastric environment.
AI.result: Demonstrated week-long stable gastric residence, continuous real-time telemetry of gastric radiation exposure, early detection of dose accumulation, and safe GI passage after triggered disassembly in swine studies.
AI.conclusion: Kirigami-enabled electronic integration is a scalable strategy for long-term gastric-resident robotic systems, offering a promising in vivo alternative to wearable or handheld dosimeters.

title: Absolute Stability of Nonlinear Negative Imaginary Systems with Application to Potential Energy Shaping
summary: This paper establishes absolute stability conditions for nonlinear negative imaginary (NI) systems interconnected with static nonlinear feedback. We first show that the NI property is preserved when the feedback nonlinearity can be expressed as the gradient of a continuously differentiable function, and the composite storage of the resulting system remains positive definite. This condition provides a direct connection between nonlinear static feedback and storage-function shaping along the measured output channels. Building on this result, conditions are derived for absolute stability of the closed-loop system under mild assumptions. The linear specialization of the results strictly generalizes prior absolute stability results for linear NI systems, allowing coupled nonlinearities not covered by existing slope-restricted or sector-bounded frameworks. Finally, the proposed theory is illustrated through a linear example highlighting this generalization and a nonlinear example that shows the utility of the proposed results in potential energy shaping.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes absolute stability conditions for nonlinear negative imaginary (NI) systems interconnected with static nonlinear feedback, showing the NI property is preserved when feedback nonlinearity is a gradient of a continuously differentiable function.
AI.motivation: To extend absolute stability results for linear NI systems to nonlinear NI systems with static nonlinear feedback, addressing coupled nonlinearities not covered by existing slope-restricted or sector-bounded frameworks.
AI.method: The authors prove that the NI property is preserved when the feedback nonlinearity is expressible as the gradient of a continuously differentiable function with positive definite composite storage. From this, they derive absolute stability conditions under mild assumptions.
AI.result: The linear specialization strictly generalizes prior absolute stability results for linear NI systems, and the theory is validated through a linear example showing generalization and a nonlinear example demonstrating utility in potential energy shaping.
AI.conclusion: The proposed conditions enable absolute stability analysis for a broader class of nonlinear NI feedback interconnections, with applications to potential energy shaping.

title: Synthesis of Limit Cycles and Reference Tracking via Switching Affine Systems
summary: This paper introduces a novel method to approximate limit cycles of nonlinear ODEs by use of switching affine dynamics in order to ease data-based modeling and analysis. Previous approaches to approximating limit cycles by switching systems have been largely confined to simple partitions into two-regions or low-dimensional (often planar) settings. In contrast, this study utilizes more general partitions in higher-dimensional state spaces, augmented by external signals, to develop a synthesis scheme that guarantees a globally stable limit cycle. The synthesis task is formulated and solved based on constrained numerical optimization. Starting from sampled data of the nonlinear dynamics, the method minimizes the error between the data and the limit cycle generated by the switching affine model, while employing stability constraints to ensure global stability. Based on the obtained model, the paper tackles the problem of reference tracking for switching affine systems with periodic behavior. While the approximation scheme is based on a common Lyapunov function, the reference tracking approach uses multiple Lyapunov functions to achieve less conservative convergence results. The principle and effectiveness of the proposed methods are illustrated through a set of examples.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a method to approximate limit cycles of nonlinear ODEs using switching affine dynamics with general partitions in higher-dimensional spaces, enforced by constrained numerical optimization and stability constraints. It also addresses reference tracking for such systems using multiple Lyapunov functions for less conservative convergence.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches to approximating limit cycles via switching systems are limited to simple two-region or low-dimensional (often planar) settings, which restricts their applicability to more complex, higher-dimensional nonlinear systems.
AI.method: The method uses more general partitions in higher-dimensional state spaces augmented by external signals, formulates the synthesis as a constrained numerical optimization problem that minimizes error between sampled data and the switching affine model's limit cycle, and enforces global stability via stability constraints. Reference tracking employs multiple Lyapunov functions for less conservative convergence.
AI.result: The method is illustrated through a set of examples, demonstrating its ability to approximate limit cycles and achieve reference tracking for switching affine systems with periodic behavior.
AI.conclusion: The proposed switching affine approximation scheme enables data-based modeling and analysis of nonlinear ODE limit cycles in higher-dimensional settings, with global stability guarantees and improved reference tracking via multiple Lyapunov functions.

title: Residual-Corrected Equivalent-Circuit Model with Universal Differential Equations for Robust Battery Voltage Prediction under Operating-Condition Shift
summary: Accurate terminal-voltage prediction underpins model-based battery management, yet low-order equivalent-circuit models (\ecm{}) lack expressiveness under transient conditions, whereas purely data-driven predictors sacrifice interpretability and may degrade under operating-condition shift. This paper introduces a residual-corrected hybrid formulation in which a first-order Thevenin \ecm{} (\ecmrc{}) provides the dominant voltage structure, and a compact neural network embedded as a universal differential equation (\ude{}) corrects only the latent polarization mismatch. The \ecmrc{} parameters identified by nonlinear least squares warm-start the hybrid model so that the learned component operates in a low-residual regime. Experiments on a public Panasonic 18650PF dataset compare the proposed \ecmude{} with standalone \ecmrc{} and Long Short-Term Memory (\lstm{}) baselines across four axes: matched-condition prediction on UDDS at \SI{25}{\celsius}, inference-time perturbation of the supplied state-of-charge (\SOC{}, denoted $z$) input, zero-shot temperature transfer (\SI{25}{\celsius} to \SI{-20}{\celsius}), and zero-shot drive-cycle transfer to US06, LA92, and HWFET. The proposed \ecmude{} achieves the lowest voltage error in every setting, reducing mean absolute error (\mae{}) by 48\% relative to the \lstm{} under matched conditions and showing an order-of-magnitude lower inter-seed variability (coefficient of variation: 0.44\% vs.\ 6.20\%). Substantial gains persist under challenging distribution shifts, indicating that the physical model anchors prediction where a purely learned model is most vulnerable. These results position residual-corrected \ecmude{} as a lightweight and interpretable enhancement of low-order circuit models for voltage prediction in battery management systems (\bms{}).

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid battery voltage prediction model combining a first-order Thevenin equivalent-circuit model (ECM) with a neural-network-based universal differential equation (UDE) for residual correction. The ECM provides the dominant voltage structure, while the compact neural network corrects latent polarization mismatch. The hybrid model (ECM-UDE) outperforms standalone ECM and LSTM baselines across matched-condition prediction, SOC perturbation, zero-shot temperature transfer (25°C to -20°C), and zero-shot drive-cycle transfer, reducing MAE by 48% over LSTM with dramatically lower variability (CV 0.44% vs 6.20%).
AI.motivation: Low-order equivalent-circuit models lack expressiveness under transient conditions, while purely data-driven predictors sacrifice interpretability and degrade under operating-condition shift. This work aims to combine the interpretability and robustness of physical models with the expressiveness of neural networks for accurate and reliable battery voltage prediction.
AI.method: A residual-corrected hybrid formulation (ECM-UDE) where a first-order Thevenin ECM (ECMrc) provides the dominant voltage structure, and a compact neural network embedded as a universal differential equation (UDE) corrects only the latent polarization mismatch. ECMrc parameters are identified by nonlinear least squares to warm-start the hybrid model, ensuring the learned component operates in a low-residual regime.
AI.result: ECM-UDE achieves the lowest voltage error in every setting: 48% MAE reduction over LSTM under matched conditions, order-of-magnitude lower inter-seed variability (CV 0.44% vs 6.20%), and substantial gains under zero-shot temperature transfer (25°C to -20°C) and drive-cycle transfer (US06, LA92, HWFET).
AI.conclusion: Residual-corrected ECM-UDE is a lightweight and interpretable enhancement of low-order circuit models for voltage prediction in battery management systems, with the physical model anchoring prediction where purely learned models are most vulnerable.

title: Distributed Online Learning for Time-Critical Communication in 6G Industrial Subnetworks
summary: 6G industrial in-X subnetworks are expected to support highly time-critical alarm reporting in large-scale environments characterized by mobility, bursty event-driven traffic, and limited radio resources. In such settings, conventional medium access solutions are ill-suited to guarantee reliable delivery of critical traffic, e.g., emergency alarms, within strict deadlines, especially when multiple subnetworks become simultaneously active after a common alarm event, a scenario widely referred as medium access with a shared message. This paper proposes a distributed deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based medium access control protocol for timely alarm transmission in time-critical industrial subnetworks. The proposed method enables each local access point (LAP) to learn, in an online manner, to infer contention conditions from a broadcast contention-signature signal and to autonomously select a transmission pattern over the available channels using a lightweight deep neural network and an (ephsilon)-greedy policy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently achieves a higher probability of in-time alarm delivery than benchmark random-access schemes, while exhibiting better scalability with increasing network density. For instance, the proposed method improves probability of in-time alarm delivery by at least 7% with a network size of 40 subnetworks, while the gain increases to 21% when the number of subnetworks increases to 60.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a distributed DRL-based MAC protocol for time-critical alarm reporting in 6G industrial in-X subnetworks. Each local access point learns to infer contention from a broadcast contention-signature signal and autonomously selects transmission patterns using a lightweight DNN and ε-greedy policy. The method achieves higher in-time alarm delivery probability (7-21% improvement) compared to benchmark schemes, with better scalability as network density increases.
AI.motivation: Conventional medium access solutions are ill-suited to guarantee reliable delivery of critical traffic (e.g., emergency alarms) within strict deadlines in large-scale industrial environments characterized by mobility, bursty event-driven traffic, limited radio resources, and scenarios where multiple subnetworks become simultaneously active after a common alarm event (medium access with a shared message).
AI.method: A distributed deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based medium access control protocol where each local access point (LAP) learns online to infer contention conditions from a broadcast contention-signature signal and autonomously selects transmission patterns over available channels using a lightweight deep neural network and an ε-greedy policy.
AI.result: The proposed approach consistently achieves higher probability of in-time alarm delivery than benchmark random-access schemes, with better scalability. Improvement is at least 7% with 40 subnetworks and 21% with 60 subnetworks.
AI.conclusion: The DRL-based distributed MAC protocol effectively addresses the challenge of timely alarm transmission in time-critical industrial subnetworks, outperforming conventional random-access schemes particularly under dense network conditions.

title: Probabilistic Assessment of Rare Transient Instability Events via Kriging-based Active Learning Framework
comment: Accepted by International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems for future publication
summary: The increasing uncertainty in modern power systems, driven by the integration of intermittent energy sources and variable loads, underscores the need for probabilistic transient stability assessment. However, existing assessment methods primarily focus on average system stability behavior and may struggle or incur high computational cost when identifying rare transient instability events, which in turn are critical for ensuring system resilience. To address this, the paper proposes a Kriging-based active learning framework to accurately characterize rare instability regions within the input uncertainty space and estimate the associated small instability probability, while requiring only a limited number of expensive time-domain simulations. The proposed active learning (AL) framework is tested on a modified IEEE 59-bus system with simulated load and wind uncertainties, and a WECC 240-bus system incorporating real-world wind and solar generation data. Comparative studies with the existing random forest-based active learning method and three non-AL methods demonstrate that the proposed AL framework achieves superior accuracy and computational efficiency.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Kriging-based active learning framework for probabilistic transient stability assessment that efficiently identifies rare instability regions and estimates small instability probabilities with limited time-domain simulations, outperforming existing methods on IEEE 59-bus and WECC 240-bus systems.
AI.motivation: Existing probabilistic transient stability assessment methods focus on average behavior and struggle with high computational cost when identifying rare transient instability events, which are critical for system resilience under increasing uncertainty from intermittent energy sources and variable loads.
AI.method: A Kriging-based active learning framework is proposed to characterize rare instability regions in the input uncertainty space and estimate small instability probabilities, requiring only a limited number of expensive time-domain simulations.
AI.result: Tested on a modified IEEE 59-bus system and a WECC 240-bus system, the proposed framework achieved superior accuracy and computational efficiency compared to random forest-based active learning and three non-active learning methods.
AI.conclusion: The Kriging-based active learning framework effectively and efficiently addresses the challenge of rare transient instability event identification in probabilistic transient stability assessment, improving system resilience analysis.

title: Quantifying Trade-Offs Between Stability and Goal-Obfuscation
summary: Safety-critical autonomy in adversarial settings demands more than Lyapunov stability of tracking error signals. An agent executing a goal-directed trajectory is intrinsically legible to a passive observer running online Bayesian inference, because the contractive dynamics of any Lyapunov basin of attraction concentrates posterior belief over the latent intent parameters. We initiates the study of intent privacy over a continuous state space as a joint control problem on the physical state combined with the latent belief state of a putative observer. With the main challenges concentrated around the analysis of the belief-state dynamics, the agent dynamics is assumed to be simple, modeled by the differential inclusion $\dot{x}\in u+\bar{d}\mathbb{B}$. That is, the agent is fully actuated with bounded unknown disturbance to the control input. The observer's intent inference process is modeled as a discrete-time stochastic dynamical system evolving over the belief state space of a Rao Blackwellized particle filter reasoning over large random samples of possible agent goals. The agent's control input is modeled as a piecewise constant signal, with jumps matching the RBPF update times. Building on a prior intent-inference framework and its KL-based information leakage measurement, a privacy constraint is imposed, which amounts to maintaining information leakage above a prescribed threshold with high probability, using probabilistic discrete-time control barrier functions. A key technical contribution is the derivation of separate PCBF results for the Bayesian update step and the resampling step of the RBPF, enabling a PCBF result for the full update as well as integration of the privacy constraint with the agent's task-side tracking requirement. Finally, a joint feasibility analysis is carried out by examining the interplay between the privacy constraint and the tracking envelope.

AI.tldr: This paper studies intent privacy in safety-critical autonomous systems, framing it as a joint control problem over physical state and observer belief state. Using Rao-Blackwellized particle filters for intent inference and probabilistic control barrier functions, the authors derive constraints to maintain information leakage above a threshold while preserving task tracking performance.
AI.motivation: Safety-critical autonomy in adversarial settings requires more than Lyapunov stability of tracking errors; goal-directed trajectories are intrinsically legible to observers running Bayesian inference, necessitating formal study of intent privacy.
AI.method: Models the problem as joint control over physical state (fully actuated with bounded disturbance) and observer belief state (discrete-time RBPF dynamics). Imposes privacy constraints via probabilistic discrete-time control barrier functions (PCBF) applied separately to Bayesian update and resampling steps of the RBPF.
AI.result: Derives separate PCBF results for Bayesian update and resampling steps, enabling a full PCBF for the joint update. Performs joint feasibility analysis examining interplay between privacy constraint and tracking envelope.
AI.conclusion: The PCBF framework successfully integrates intent privacy constraints with task-side tracking requirements in continuous state spaces, validated through joint feasibility analysis.
